I added the missing `break;` after the inner `switch` in the `number`, `dateTime`, `boolean`, `array` and `object` branches of `executeFilterCondition`. The filter tests pass (226 of 226) and the type-check is clean. The linter couldn't run here.

Without the `break`, an operation that wasn't handled in one type's switch fell through into the next type's code. For example, a `number` condition with the operation `after` ended up in the `dateTime` code and called `.toMillis()` on a number, which throws a `TypeError`. After the fix, those cases reach the existing "Unknown filter parameter operator" warning and return `false`. The change is in `packages/workflow/src/node-parameters/filter-parameter.ts`.

I added a parameterized test in `test/filter-parameter.test.ts`. It checks that an unsupported operation on each of the four types (number, dateTime, boolean, array) returns `false` instead of falling through. I didn't run it against the old code.

## fix(core): Add missing break statements in filter condition evaluation

Added missing `break;` after the inner operation switch in the number, dateTime, boolean, array and object cases of executeFilterCondition in filter-parameter.ts. An unhandled operation for a type previously fell through into the next type's code (e.g. number with 'after' reached the dateTime code and threw on .toMillis()). It now reaches the 'Unknown filter parameter operator' warning and returns false. Added a parameterized test for unsupported operations on number, dateTime, boolean and array.

### What changed
- 1 source file(s), 1 test file(s), 29 changed lines
- `packages/workflow/src/node-parameters/filter-parameter.ts`

### What ran
- The agent ran the tests 2 time(s) and says: acdc-test test/filter-parameter.test.ts: 226 of 226 passed. The first run had one failure in my new test, caused by an invalid test input, which I fixed. acdc-typecheck: no errors. acdc-lint: could not run (tsgolint executable not found in this environment), so lint was not verified.
- Type check: passes; lint: not available for this commit
- Tests for the issue: 1/1; tests that passed before: 235/235

### Risks that remain
- Change risk: medium (14% chance of a revert or follow-up fix, from n8n's history)
- Any workflow that relied on the old fall-through would now get false plus a warning instead of an exception or accidental match. This looks unlikely, since the old behavior was mostly a TypeError.
- The new test uses `as unknown as FilterConditionValue` casts to build invalid operations.
- I did not run the new test against the unfixed code, so I haven't confirmed it fails there.
- Lint was not run.
